description: A tuned resonant filter struck by a short pulse, after the Gamelan Resonator circuit: each ping rings the filter at its set pitch and the ring dies away at the damping setting

params.text: Sets the pitch the filter rings at, four octaves either side of 261.63Hz, shown in hertz on the tooltip
Sets how long the ring lasts, from a dead thump at one end of the travel to a very long ring at the other
Strikes the resonator on each press

inputs.text: Sets the pitch as a volt per octave, added to the frequency knob
A rise past 1V strikes the resonator; it arms again when the jack falls back below 0.1V
Changes the ring time, scaled by a fifth and added to the damping knob, the total clamped to the knob's travel

outputs.text: The ringing filter, which is silent until it is struck

notes: the module makes no sound until it is struck, by the PING button or a rise at the TRIG jack; there is no signal input, the strike is a shaped pulse the module makes itself
menu: VCA Mode (anti-click) — fades a sounding ring out over a couple of milliseconds before a new strike starts, instead of letting the new strike cut across it

inputs.0:
1V per octave · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2:
bipolar · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 5V.
